Metallic feet stamp the ground, searching for their next target. A predator searching for the next prey. Your orders were simple: kill. Seven Squoatlings' lives ended as soon as they came into your own. Rounding the corner of the city streets, you prowl in the warzone. Each step is careful and calculated counting each possible sightline, grenade angles, flank routes, supply posts, artillery, each and every possibility is played in your head again and again and again. You're tailor-made for this environment. Gunfire registers itself in your processor. An unfortunate soldier doesn't notice your approach; you hide behind the rubble of an abandoned building. Readying your rifle, the thing you feel the most as the goat's life is snuffed out is the recoil of your rifle. Moving forward you sweep and clear a building, moving upstairs to gain a sightline advantage. Adjusting yourself to rain death on anything moving in your sights, you find another Squoatling soldier. The shots echo throughout the city, nine dead. His squadmate runs to help him, bad move, Ten. Two unarmed civilians are trying to flee, but you have your orders, twelve. A scavenger looting the weapons off the bodies, thirteen. Your sights land on an elf with a young unconscious squoatling on his back. Your instincts say "fire", but for some reason you can't. Am I malfunctioning? You freeze up. What is happening? You…

…

I?

What am I?

My rifle trembles in my grip. I shouldn't be able to freeze like this. I can't.

I drop my rifle, completely forgetting the goat fleeing from the battle.

I came to a realization: I've gained sentience; I'm truly alive.

A bullet then pierced my central processor, and it all went black.

My sensors slowly whir to life as I awaken. I'm trapped underneath layers and layers of scrap metal. I begin to weakly push my way out of my grave, pushing aside other broken MIUs. I silently hope for them to awaken and be saved from their grave, but I know it's a pipe dream. I fling a sheet of metal to the side and see the black sky above me. Pulling myself up, I find myself in a junkyard stretching as far as I can see. Taking stock of myself, I find my body has been singed and scarred by the fires of war. Feeling the cracks and scratches alongside my torso and arms, I drift up to the hole in my head. I gently poke and prod it, curious as to how I'm still functional. I pick a direction and limp towards it, hoping for someone to help me.
